chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate food with a group of people, he was the first to place his hand and the last to raise it, so that the people could eat.
ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic etiquette for eating with a group of people?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) embodiment of *adab* (etiquette) by prioritizing the comfort of his companions over his own appetite, a practice deeply valued in Shia jurisprudence as a model for social conduct. This deliberate delay in finishing his meal served to alleviate any pressure on guests to rush, thereby fostering an atmosphere of generosity and mutual respect during communal dining.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ate food with a people, was the first one to place his<sup>saww</sup> hand, and the last one to raise it, to let the people (finish) eating’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal f, ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when eating food with a people would, as the first one, begin eating and be the last to stop it, so that the people complete eating.’”
